MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  November 13, 2018

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Sachs at 5:02 p.m., on November 13, 2018, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on November 8, 2018, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Sachs

Absent:  Council Member Bucknum

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

Liability Claims; Claimants: Noval and Donaldson; Agency Claimed Against – City of
Mission Viejo and; Significant Exposure to Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (2) of
Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9. (2 cases)

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

Mayor Sachs recessed the meeting to Closed Session at the hour of 5:02 p.m. The City Council
reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with four Council Members present (Council Member Bucknum was
absent).

City Council Minutes  1  November 13, 2018
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council reviewed claims against the city and gave
direction to staff but no reportable actions occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Sachs

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Proclaim November 12 through 18, 2018 To Be "National Nurse Practitioner Week"

  Mayor Sachs presented the proclamation to Nurse Practitioner Bita Kodi.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Bill Moorhead, M.V.: thanked the people who voted for him for Director of Moulton Niguel Water
District and said he hopes to earn the trust of those who did not vote for him. He also thanked the
Council for the City’s sign program which, he said, makes it very easy for candidates to know
where they can and cannot place their campaign signs.

Shayan Ahmad, M.V.: representing the Community of Character, he announced that the character
theme for the month of November is thankfulness and the representative film, It Could Happen to
You, will be shown on Sunday, November 18 at 2:00 p.m. in the City Council Chamber.

Nancy Larkin, M.V.: expressed concern with a book in the Mission Viejo Library that is graphic
in nature and sits in close proximity to small children. She asked that the book be moved to a
location where patrons would have to request it.

Juan Gonzales, representing Southern California Gas (SCE): congratulated the Council Members
who were re-elected and discussed “all electric” state legislation. He said that SCE does not support
this and believes in a customer’s right to choose electric, solar or other options. He further
discussed SCE's efforts to reduce greenhouse gases.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Bucknum

City Council Minutes  2  November 13, 2018
 1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of October 23, 2018, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated October 12, 2018 in the Amount of $2,614,106.96

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated October 19, 2018 in the Amount of $688,446.52

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated October 26, 2018 in the Amount of $1,092,001.40

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for September 2018

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for September 2018

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
  September 2018

  Received and filed.

8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for September 2018

  Received and filed.

9.  Transmittal of Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the quarter ending September 30, 2018

  Received and filed the accompanying Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the Quarter ending
  September 30, 2018.

10.  Biennial City Commission Member Term Expiration

  (1) Directed the City Clerk to post the Notice of City Commission vacancies, (2) set
  application deadline for December 21, 2018, and (3) scheduled appointment of
  Commission Members for January 8, 2019.

City Council Minutes  3  November 13, 2018
 11.  Security Lighting – Cordova Park/Arroyo Trail and Lakeside Park

  (1) Approved Contract Amendment #3 in the amount of $89,200 to the existing Park
  Hardscape Contract with S. Parker Engineering, Inc. for the installation of security light
  foundations at Cordova Park/Arroyo Trail and Lakeside Park; and (2) adopted Resolution
  18-28 Amending the current FY 2018/19 Budget.

12.  Fourth Amendment to OCFA Joint Powers Authority Agreement

  Approved and directed the Mayor to execute the submitted Fourth Amendment to the
  Amended Orange County Fire Authority JPA Agreement.

13.  Marty Russo Youth Athletic Park Accessible Ramp Improvements

  Adopted Resolution 18-29 Amending the Fiscal Year 2018/2019 Budget to Create Capital
  Improvement Project 19313 to Construct the Marty Russo Youth Athletic Park Accessible
  Ramp Improvements

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

NEW BUSINESS

14.  Consolidation of the City’s 457(b) and 401(a) record-keeping platforms with two
  different providers to a single record-keeping platform with Nationwide.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Sachs, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 18-30 Authorizing Staff to Consolidate the City’s 457(b) and 401(a) Record-
  keeping Platforms with Two Different Providers to a Single Record-keeping Platform with
  Nationwide and Authorize the City Manager to Sign All Required Provider Agreements on
  Behalf of the City; (2) adopt Resolution 18-31 Approving the Creation of a Deferred
  Compensation Investment Committee; and (3) consider including the Chair or Vice Chair
  of the Investment Advisory Committee as a member of the Deferred Compensation
  Investment Committee (in an advisory capacity).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

15.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Sachs deferred his time for Chief Capobianco's report (item #19).
City Council Minutes  4  November 13, 2018
 16.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Council Member Bucknum was absent so the report was deferred to the next meeting.

17.  Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Sachs deferred the report to a future meeting.

18.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Council Member Bucknum was absent so the report was deferred to the next meeting.

STAFF REPORTS

19.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Update from Chief Capobianco

  Chief Capobianco discussed OCFA's oversight efforts during the current fire season. He
  described the routine threat evaluations and OCFA’s equipment and crew positioning
  which are ready for callout at any time.

Lt. Vuong discussed the deployment of Orange County Sheriff’s Department Response Teams to
help with evacuations and security at the Woolsey fires.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

20.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum was absent.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell thanked Chief Capobianco and Lieutenant Vuong for their reports and
said he is grateful for their work. He outlined his attendance at the City of Tustin's State of the City
and the grand openings for new Mission Viejo businesses including Floor and Decor and the new
neighborhood Target. He recently attended the Headquarters Battalion Marine Corps Ball, the
Wounded Warriors Amputee softball game and the City’s Veterans Day ceremony. Council
Member Goodell noted that the Olympic Promotion Committee and staff are looking for ways to
help promote existing events and create new events utilizing City facilities and the College's new
stadium. They are working on a website to promote opportunities for people to come to Mission
Viejo and will target the national governing bodies for Olympic sports, state track meets, and other
large scale sporting events. Council Member Goodell said the Committee is trying to promote
City Council Minutes  5  November 13, 2018
 Mission Viejo as a place to come play, stay and spend money. He said the Economic Development
Committee will also be meeting soon and they are discussing exciting ways to support more hotel
opportunities, embrace changes in the retail environment and move forward with plans for the
community core project.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that the holiday toy drive for the City’s adopted Marine
battalion will begin soon. New, unwrapped toys can be dropped off in designated boxes at City
Hall, the Library, Sierra Recreation Center, Montanoso Recreation Center, the Tennis Pavilion and
Norman P. Murray Community Center. Donations can also be made via checks made payable to
the Mission Viejo Community Foundation. Council Member Kelley announced that she attended
the Marine Corps ball and it was gratifying to know that some of the Marines were able to attend
the event because of the City’s fundraising efforts. She also attended the grand opening of the new
small format Target store on Puerta Real as well as Hometown Halloween, a candlelight vigil for
the victims of the Pittsburgh massacre, the Wounded Warriors softball game, and both Mission
Viejo’s and El Toro Cemetery’s Veterans Day events. She thanked all veterans and her veteran
colleagues, Mayor Ed Sachs and Mayor Pro Tem Greg Raths for their service. In closing, Council
Member Kelley discussed the Community of Character word for the month, thankfulness, and read
a quote from Charles Swindoll: “Life is 10 percent what happens to me and 90 percent how I react
to it.”

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths thanked voters for re-electing him to another term as Council Member. He
also thanked the Cal State Fullerton student who came out to watch the Council meeting. He said
he had a great week with the Marine Corps birthday and Veterans Day ceremony and he enjoyed
his time at the Marine Corps Ball. Mayor Pro Tem Raths expressed his appreciation for all that the
City has done for veterans in Mission Viejo and he thanked Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay
for getting a wall painted on Muirlands Boulevard, updating slopes around town, and getting the
City ready for Christmas with beautiful lights and decor.

Mayor Sachs

Mayor Sachs discussed Mission Viejo’s candlelight vigil in response to the Pittsburgh massacre
and said it truly was gratifying to see 250-300 people in attendance. He congratulated the City for
winning the 2018 Project of the Year Award from the Southern California Public Works
Association for the Marguerite Aquatics Complex. Mayor Sachs said with the current fires, he
thought it was important to bring up his recent trip to the White House. While there, he and Council
Member Bucknum were able to meet with several Secretaries, including Secretary of the Interior
Zinke. He said there seems to be a spat between the President and California’s Governor regarding
wildfires and fuel modification. He stated that they are both right and there can be a better job done
with forestry efforts but down in Southern California, the issues are different and mitigation needs
to continue. Mayor Sachs noted that he is very proud of Orange County Fire Authority’s efforts
and he thanked firefighters across the state and from other states who are coming in to help. He
also shared that a converted 747 airplane is now being used to drop water on some of the fire areas.

City Council Minutes  6  November 13, 2018
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:08 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Sachs adjourned the meeting in memory of Council Member Bucknum's mother, Barbara
Ann Maynard, to Tuesday, November 27, 2018, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of November 27, 2018

City Council Minutes  7  November 13, 2018
